questions.q: A Christian scholar asked whether Islam has a teaching like “Love your enemy.” Which idea from the Quran (41:34) did the author give in reply?
options: Keep away from enemies until they apologise
The verse asks for a positive response from your side first, not waiting.
Enmity is natural and must simply be endured
The article says friendship is natural and enmity is unnatural, born of misunderstanding.
Return good for evil, and the enemy may become your dearest friend
Yes. The verse treats an enemy as a potential friend, to be won by a positive response.
Treat enemies exactly as they treat you
The verse says good and evil deeds are not equal; it asks for good in return for bad.
questions.rationale: The author quoted 41:34 – “Do good deeds in return for bad deeds; then you will see that the one who was once your enemy has become your dearest friend” – and concluded that your enemy is your potential friend.

questions.q: The article uses the example of a cow turning grass into milk. What is it meant to show?
options: That simple living is better than modern life
Not quite. The article says: That a person can convert negative experiences into positive thinking.
That a person can convert negative experiences into positive thinking
Well done. This “art of conversion” is called the gist of prayer and spirituality.
That animals are closer to nature than man
Not quite. The article says: That a person can convert negative experiences into positive thinking.
That good results need a long time
Not quite. The article says: That a person can convert negative experiences into positive thinking.
questions.rationale: “If a cow can convert the grass that it eats into milk, why cannot man, with a mind a billion times more developed… convert negativity into positivity?”

questions.article: All Praise Is Due to God
questions.q: According to the article, what is the one thing man can offer to God?
options: Long hours of ritual
Not quite. The article says: Acknowledgment of His greatness and bounties.
Knowledge gathered over a lifetime
Not quite. The article says: Acknowledgment of His greatness and bounties.
Wealth spent in His name
Not quite. The article says: Acknowledgment of His greatness and bounties.
Acknowledgment of His greatness and bounties
Right. God is too great for man to give Him anything else.
questions.rationale: “God the Almighty is too great for man to give Him anything. The only thing man can offer in His presence is acknowledgment.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, did the Creator bring the universe into being through a long process of cause and effect rather than by a sudden miracle?
options: So that the prophets could arrive in the right order
Not quite. The article says: So that man could develop his thinking and creativity, giving rise to science and civilization.
So that man could develop his thinking and creativity, giving rise to science and civilization
Exactly. A gradual, law-bound world is one man can study and learn from.
So that the earth would have time to cool
Not quite. The article says: So that man could develop his thinking and creativity, giving rise to science and civilization.
Because a miracle would have been beyond the laws of nature
Not quite. The article says: So that man could develop his thinking and creativity, giving rise to science and civilization.
questions.rationale: The article says that had the universe been created suddenly, “creativity could not have been developed in man. No science, no civilization would have come into existence.”

questions.q: “One person’s duty is another’s right.” What follows from this, in the article’s view?
options: Rights must be won before duties can be asked for
Not quite. The article says: If everyone fulfils their duties, everyone’s rights are taken care of automatically.
If everyone fulfils their duties, everyone’s rights are taken care of automatically
Yes. That is why the stress is placed on duty.
Duties and rights can never be balanced
Not quite. The article says: If everyone fulfils their duties, everyone’s rights are taken care of automatically.
Only governments can secure people’s rights
Not quite. The article says: If everyone fulfils their duties, everyone’s rights are taken care of automatically.
questions.rationale: The article says, “if we all follow the principle of being duty conscious, automatically our rights will be taken care of,” and that rights should be asked for from God.

questions.q: At the time of the Prophet’s death, in what state did the Quran exist?
options: Written in full, but memorized by only a few scribes
Not quite. The article says: Complete in the memories of companions in its present order, and fully written down on separate materials.
Complete in the memories of companions in its present order, and fully written down on separate materials
Correct. The order lived in memory; all the parts existed in writing.
As one bound volume kept in the mosque at Medina
Not quite. The article says: Complete in the memories of companions in its present order, and fully written down on separate materials.
Only in memory, with nothing yet written
Not quite. The article says: Complete in the memories of companions in its present order, and fully written down on separate materials.
questions.rationale: “The order existed in memory, not in writing, though all the parts existed at that time in written form.”

questions.q: The article describes Zaid ibn Thabit’s work under Abu Bakr as “more of collection than of compilation.” Why?
options: He chose which verses were to be included
Not quite. The article says: He gathered the written pieces and cross-checked them against the memorized Quran before writing it out in order.
He translated the verses for new Muslims
Not quite. The article says: He gathered the written pieces and cross-checked them against the memorized Quran before writing it out in order.
He gathered the written pieces and cross-checked them against the memorized Quran before writing it out in order
Well reasoned. The written and oral forms were matched first.
He arranged the chapters in a new order of his own
Not quite. The article says: He gathered the written pieces and cross-checked them against the memorized Quran before writing it out in order.
questions.rationale: The scattered written pieces were “used to crosscheck countless memories in oral tradition”; once the two matched, Zaid wrote the verses down in their correct order.

questions.q: American researchers compared winning and losing wrestlers of equal strength and training. What separated them?
options: Their diet and hours of sleep
Not quite. The article says: Their state of mind: winners were positive, relaxed and confident.
Their years of experience
Not quite. The article says: Their state of mind: winners were positive, relaxed and confident.
Their state of mind: winners were positive, relaxed and confident
Right. The difference was psychological, not physical.
The quality of their coaches
Not quite. The article says: Their state of mind: winners were positive, relaxed and confident.
questions.rationale: The report said: “Losers tended to be more depressed and confused before competing, while the winners were positive and relaxed.”

questions.q: The Prophet said “Perform your prayer as you see me performing it,” but gave no such instruction about government. What does the article conclude from this?
options: The Medina state must be copied in every age
Not quite. The article says: Worship has a fixed pattern, while politics is to be shaped by the social conditions of the time.
Politics is forbidden to believers
Not quite. The article says: Worship has a fixed pattern, while politics is to be shaped by the social conditions of the time.
Rulers should always be religious scholars
Not quite. The article says: Worship has a fixed pattern, while politics is to be shaped by the social conditions of the time.
Worship has a fixed pattern, while politics is to be shaped by the social conditions of the time
Yes. The article calls this “situational politics.”
questions.rationale: “Islamic ibadah has a set pattern forever but Islamic politics has no such eternal norms… a kind of situational politics that is based on social realities.”

questions.q: The Quraysh mocked the Prophet with the name “Muzammam” (the condemned). How did he respond?
options: He left Makkah the same day
Not quite. The article says: Calmly – he said their abuse was aimed at “Muzammam,” whereas he was Muhammad.
He answered them with equal insults
Not quite. The article says: Calmly – he said their abuse was aimed at “Muzammam,” whereas he was Muhammad.
He asked his companions to punish them
Not quite. The article says: Calmly – he said their abuse was aimed at “Muzammam,” whereas he was Muhammad.
Calmly – he said their abuse was aimed at “Muzammam,” whereas he was Muhammad
Exactly. He refused to be provoked.
questions.rationale: The Prophet said: “They abuse a person by the name of Muzammam. Whereas I am Muhammad.” The article concludes that Islam does not teach one to be easily provoked.
